How to Ban Players on Your Counter-Strike 2 Server
kickid Command Help & Examples - Total CS
banid Command Help & Examples - Total CS
banned_user.cfg and banned_ip.cfg file format help

notes: Standard Valve Source RCON on the game server's own TCP port, default 27015, so there is no separate RCON port setting. RCON is off unless the server is launched with -usercon AND rcon_password is non-empty: the Pterodactyl CS2 egg appends ' -usercon' only when RCON is enabled and always passes +rcon_password, and the joedwards32/CS2 container exposes CS2_RCONPW with CS2_PORT=27015. The dedicated server installs from app 730 itself (steamcmd +app_update 730), not from a separate server app as with CS:GO's 740. IDENTIFIER WARNING, the weakest part of this file: it moderates by Steam ID, but every source consulted documents kickid and banid taking the userid from status. Total CS gives 'kickid <User ID> <Message>' and, for banid, 'Accepts user ID, not Steam ID'; Wasabi Hosting gives 'Kick a player by userid (from status, safer than names)'; XGamingServer gives 'banid <minutes> <userid>' and says to find the user ID with status first. Only Loafhosts shows a Steam ID form, and only for ban (banid 0 STEAM_0:1:12345). No source consulted shows kickid accepting a Steam ID. The Steam ID templates are kept for two reasons: writeid demonstrably emits 'banid 0 STEAM_1:0:xxxx' lines into banned_user.cfg, which is then exec'd back through the console, so banid must parse a Steam ID; and the Source engine's kickid and banid are declared as taking 'userid | uniqueid'. That second point is engine knowledge, not a citation. Steam ID is preferred over userid regardless because userids are reassigned on every connection, so a userid captured when the roster was listed can address a different player by the time a kick is sent. If the engine knowledge is wrong, kick silently targets nobody, so verify kick against a live server first. removeid is the one command two sources agree takes a Steam ID (XGamingServer 'removeid <steamid>', Loafhosts 'removeid STEAM_0:1:12345'). Ban persistence is the other weak claim: banid only records the ban in memory and it is lost on restart unless writeid flushes it to game/csgo/cfg/banned_user.cfg, which must in turn be exec'd from server.cfg to load at boot (XGamingServer); Wasabi Hosting warns that 'legacy Source ban commands like banid/writeid have been unreliable in some CS2 builds' and recommends a plugin-based admin system (CounterStrikeSharp/SourceMod-style) for durable bans. The '; writeid' chained onto ban and unban is a construction, not a quoted form: the Source console does split a line on semicolons, but no source shows the two chained on one line over RCON, and a human would normally send them as two lines. Valve's Console Command List carries only banid ('Add a user ID to the ban list'), removeid ('Remove a user ID from the ban list') and say ('Display player message'); it does not list kickid, writeid or status, so it is thinner support than it looks. Plain 'kick' takes only a name and is avoided here because duplicate and unicode names make it ambiguous. playerParse is confirmed by no source: several sources state that server-side status lists connected players with their userids and Steam IDs (client-side status in CS2 no longer shows other players' Steam IDs, a separate well-reported change), and Valve's Status page lists the fields as userid, name, uniqueid, connection time, ping, loss, state and IP, but no source printed a real CS2 status block, so the line pattern is written loosely, a quoted or single-quoted name immediately followed by a STEAM_x:y:z id, rather than pinned to CS:GO's '# userid name uniqueid connected ping loss state rate adr' column layout. The banned_user.cfg line format is corroborated only from a Source-engine sibling title (Insurgency, app 222880), not from CS2 itself. CS2 has no motd command (CS:GO's motd.txt mechanism did not carry over), so no motd key is recorded. Confidence is low, not high: the transport and port are well corroborated by two code sources plus Valve's own page, but the identifier the kick and ban templates depend on is shown by at most one source and contradicted by three, and the roster parse is shown by none. Do not promote to high until these are run against a live server and verifiedAt is set.
